claim: For the three-edge star in Exner and Jex with two mirror arms of length \(1\), endpoint couplings \(-3/2\), one axial arm of arbitrary length \(L>0\) with endpoint coupling \(-2\), and central \(\delta\)-coupling \(\alpha\le0\), the numerically reported monotonicity transition is exactly \[\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}=\frac{2(21-e^4)}{e^4+7}=-1.090881788335\ldots.\]At this coupling the ground-state energy is exactly \(-4\) for every axial length \(L>0\), and the axial ground-state component is proportional to \(e^{2x}\). Moreover the source\'s two regimes hold globally, not just numerically: for \(\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}<\alpha\le0\) the ground-state energy decreases strictly as \(L\) increases, whereas for \(\alpha<\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}\) it increases strictly. Thus the exceptional zero-index edge is completely resolved in this model by an exact, length-independent threshold.

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the proof; numerical checks only replay the exact formulas
integrity.novelty_scope: Exact critical coupling, all-length critical branch, and global two-regime monotonicity classification for the published Exner-Jex star example.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: The general ground-state monotonicity mechanism, numerical threshold, and observation of a pure-exponential critical edge are credited to Exner and Jex.

scientific_limitations: The result is restricted to the specific mirror-symmetric three-edge star and endpoint couplings used by Exner and Jex.
It resolves the zero-index critical case for this model but not the source open problem of regime classification on arbitrary branching graphs.
Only the ground-state eigenvalue is treated; higher eigenvalues are outside the claim.
An equivalent exact simplification may exist in unindexed notes because the final derivation is elementary once the model is reduced.
title: Exact critical coupling for the Exner–Jex branching-star monotonicity transition
